children.value: This file contains a log of updates made to the MKDynamics website. It is used to track changes, additions, and improvements over time.
Ham radio: the 4NEC2 page replaces the under-construction note. It follows a 14.300 MHz dipole run in 4NEC2 5.8.16, with the symbols window, the feed-point result, and the three pattern views.
Ham radio: a Broadband Hamnet page joins the projects section. Two WRT54GL routers on firmware 3.1.0 link two laptops, and the page plays the mesh-status and HTTP clip.

Ada disassembly: AMD64, ARM64, ARM32, and i386 pages now show objdump output, with the address, the machine bytes, the instruction, and a comment, interleaved with the Ada source. Where the two integers are constants, the compiler stores the sum 8. Where the program reads the integers, the listing shows the add and Ada’s overflow check. The i386 object has no line-number table, so its three assignment lines were placed by hand.
C++ and Pascal disassembly: the built programs from the Disassembling-Binaries tree now have objdump pages. C++
add.cpp

is on AMD64, ARM64, ARM32, and i386, and each object adds the two ints. Pascal pages cover the AMD64 integer add, real add, function call, and writeln, the ARM64 integer add, multiply, real add, and function call, and the ARM32 integer add. On these Free Pascal builds INTEGER is a 16-bit Smallint. The i386 Pascal directory saves sources, and the writeln object there is a 64-bit ELF whose code matches the AMD64 writeln page.

Fortran i386 disassembly: the built programs from the Disassembling-Binaries i386 tree now have objdump pages. Integer add, multiply, and divide, real add, and the if-then are listed with the address, the machine bytes, the instruction, and a comment. Default integer and real are four bytes. The real add uses the x87 unit. The if-then reads an integer and prints when it is greater than 5.

Finite element analysis: the CAELinux page replaces the under-construction note. It follows a Salome-Meca 2015.2 session from the sketch and the extrusion through the mesh, ElmerGUI, and a displacement plot.

Power electronics: the 120 V to 12 V buck and the 50 V to 12 V buck join the power-supplies section. The 120 V page includes the passives notebook, and the 50 V page includes the inductor-core sheet. The 100 V forward converter page adds the bench photos of the TL494 timing ramp.

Finite element analysis: the OpenFOAM propulsor page links the tutorial-propeller repository, plays the 10 s mid-plane movie, and shows the efficiency, thrust, and torque plots. The mean open-water efficiency on that coarse run is 0.564 and is marked illustrative.
